approval.source: Q-73 answered 2026-10-22 (ENGINEERING_REASONING_STANDARD section 6 directive), owner's words: 'The owner-approved rule is to deduct full openings from blockwork, plaster and paint, subject to the actual construction scope.' = option A; confirmed again 2026-11-02 (AGENT_BRIEF 'Openings: full deduction of every actual opening from blockwork'; company rulebook UPC-BLOCK-OPENINGS-001)

records.rule_name: Openings are deducted per trade from one table: full actual openings from blockwork, plaster and paint; the waterproofing upturn is not deducted
records.calculation_method: per-trade opening table: SKIRTING deduct door widths (UP-CER-003); WALL_TILE gross - openings (UP-CER-005); WATERPROOFING_UPTURN no deduction (UP-WP-002 v2.0.0); PLASTER / PAINT and BLOCKWORK deduct every actual opening at its full size, no minimum size (Q-73 A), only from a face that is physically built there (no masonry, plaster or paint invented behind glazing or in a passage); reveals and returns are their own items
records.note: 1.1.0 left PLASTER_PAINT as OWNER_DECISION_PENDING (Q-OPN-1); Q-73 A answered it for blockwork, plaster and paint together (T-461 C6 (c)). 1.1.0 stays in URBAN_RULES 1.5.0 unchanged; results computed under 1.5.0 keep it
records.condition: subject to the actual construction scope: an opening is deducted from a trade only where that trade is physically built on the face

records.rule_name: Stair marble bed 1:3 mortar: theoretical cement and sand per m3 derived from the mix (calculated provisional rate)

purchasing_allowance.label: PRELIMINARY PURCHASING (owner Q-53: about 10 bags + 1.00 m3), a separate layer, never the theoretical quantity

calculation_method: dry volume = finished mortar m3 x 1.33
cement m3 = dry volume x 1 / (1 + 3); cement kg = cement m3 x 1440; bags = kg / 50 (theoretical, not rounded)
mortar m3 = stair marble area x bed thickness from the drawings / approved detail or the owner's Q-45 stair bed (0.03 m); this record gives materials per m3 only
never: the 1:4 figures (8 bags, 1.1 m3) for a 1:3 bed
a waste or bulking allowance without a named source or owner-approved allowance
the purchasing allowance reported as the theoretical quantity
a universal constant: a supplier or approved mix design replaces it
